advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Preserve prior SNAPSHOT `authorship_ledger` entries across incremental re-compaction (merge the restored ledger rather than overwriting from freshly-folded raw files only).
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:226: `compiled_state["authorship_ledger"] = _build_authorship_ledger(fold_files, ...)`
`_build_authorship_ledger` reads only `sig = ev.get("author_sig")` and `if not sig: continue` (compact.py:89-91) — a SNAPSHOT envelope has no author_sig, so its folded ledger is not carried forward
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:143-146: `candidates` lists live `.json` (excludes `.retired`), so the prior snapshot's retired raw signed events are not re-scanned either
ABSENCE: no merge of the prior snapshot's restored `authorship_ledger` (present in `compiled_state` after reduce) into the freshly-built ledger before the line-226 overwrite
advisory.finding: Incremental re-compaction silently drops previously-folded signed events from the authorship ledger. In `_compact_locked`, a prior SNAPSHOT is a KNOWN_EVENT_TYPE so it enters `parsed`/`fold_files` when foldable, but `_build_authorship_ledger(fold_files, ...)` only reads `author_sig` off each raw file (SNAPSHOTs carry none) and never re-extracts the prior snapshot's `compiled_state['authorship_ledger']`. After a second compaction, events folded into the first snapshot are no longer in any ledger, so `verify-authorship` can no longer re-verify them.
scenarios: A ticket signed under require_authenticated is compacted twice (e.g. horizon-based incremental compaction over time)
advisory.suggested_fix: When building the new ledger, also carry forward the `authorship_ledger` restored into `compiled_state` from any folded prior SNAPSHOT (union by event_uuid), in addition to scanning newly-folded raw files.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Handle ledger entries with a null epoch without misclassifying a validly-signed folded event as bad-signature (e.g. re-resolve the epoch, or classify as an infra/unknown state rather than bad-signature).
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:133-134: `else:` / `return BAD_SIGNATURE`
compact.py:98-99 records `epoch = None` on any `epoch_for_position` exception; _ledger_events sets `epoch=entry.get("epoch") if isinstance(entry.get("epoch"), int) else None` so null persists
ledger entries always have `position=None` (verify_authorship.py `_ledger_events` passes `position=None`)
advisory.finding: A ledger entry whose `epoch` was recorded as null (compaction-time `epoch_for_position` failure, or a missing `author_id`) is classified `bad-signature` at verify time, because `_verify_signed` returns BAD_SIGNATURE when both `ev.epoch is None` and `ev.position is None` (always true for ledger entries). A signed event that verified fine before compaction can thus flip to failing the merge-gate purely due to a transient lookup failure during compaction.
scenarios: Compaction runs while the identity keyring lookup transiently fails, recording a null epoch; a later verify-authorship then flags the (validly signed) folded event as bad-signature

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Detect a failed empty-tree fallback diff in `_collect_range` and error out (exit 2) rather than treating an empty result as a clean, verified scope.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:248-260: fallback `subprocess.run(...)` result is used without checking `cp.returncode`
verify_authorship.py:262: `for rel in (cp.stdout or "").splitlines():` — empty stdout ⇒ no events ⇒ gate passes
cli: `not_verified = len(events) - counts[VERIFIED]` is 0 when events is empty ⇒ exit 0 even under require_authenticated
advisory.finding: In `_collect_range`, when the primary `run_git` diff fails and the empty-tree fallback `subprocess.run(...)` ALSO fails, the return code is never checked; the code proceeds with `cp.stdout or ""` = empty, yielding zero in-scope events. Under require_authenticated an empty scope passes the gate (exit 0), so a git/environment failure produces a silent vacuous PASS rather than an error.
scenarios: CI runs verify-authorship --base <ref> where git is unavailable or the range is unresolvable and the empty-tree fallback also errors

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs `rebar verify-authorship` over an event with a present-but-invalid author_sig (tampered content and/or wrong-epoch key) and asserts exit non-zero + a `bad-signature` classification when require_authenticated is on.
evidence: verify_authorship.py: `return VERIFIED if verdict.verified else BAD_SIGNATURE`
verify_authorship.py content-binding: `if ev.payload is not None and envelope.payload != ev.payload: return BAD_SIGNATURE`
search of tests/unit for `bad-signature` yields only the held-out reducer docstring/assert on replay-never-rejects, not a verify-authorship gate assertion
AC (ticket 3183): 'the merge-gate verification flags an unsigned/unknown-author event' — only the unsigned case is asserted (test_identity_3183.py:51)
verify_authorship.py: `if not _is_identity_author(ev.author_id, tracker): return UNKNOWN_AUTHOR`
search of tests/unit for `unknown-author` yields no matches
AC names 'unknown-author event' explicitly but only 'unsigned' is asserted end-to-end
advisory.finding: The merge-gate's BAD_SIGNATURE classification path is untested. verify_authorship._verify_signed can return BAD_SIGNATURE via three distinct branches (malformed DSSE envelope, content-binding mismatch `envelope.payload != ev.payload`, and epoch verify verdict.verified False), each of which must drive a non-zero exit under require_authenticated — the actual security control. No test runs `verify-authorship` over an event carrying an author_sig that fails verification. The held-out reducer test writes a bogus author_sig but only asserts replay folds it (never rejects); it never feeds that event through the gate.
merged_from: The `unknown-author` classification is untested. _verify_signed short-circuits to UNKNOWN_AUTHOR when an event carries an author_sig but author_id does not name a valid identity ticket; _classify orders unsigned before signed-verification. No test exercises the unknown-author verdict or its contribution to the not_verified count / exit code.
scenarios: A tampered event (valid signature over different content) lands in a range; the gate must classify bad-signature and exit 1
A refactor of the content-binding or epoch-verdict branch silently drops enforcement and no test fails

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test exercising `verify-authorship --base <ref>` over a store with staged/committed event-file changes, plus an unresolvable-base (empty-tree fallback) case.
evidence: verify_authorship.py defines `_collect_range(tracker, base)` with a shallow-clone empty-tree fallback
tests invoke `["rebar", "verify-authorship", "--all"]` (test_identity_3183.py:46, test_identity_3183_heldout.py:147)
search of tests for `--base` / `_collect_range` yields no verify-authorship matches
advisory.finding: The `--base <ref>` range-scoping path (_collect_range), which is the actual CI/merge-gate invocation shape described in the module docstring, is entirely untested — including the empty-tree fallback when the base is unresolvable. All tests invoke only `--all`.
scenarios: CI runs `verify-authorship --base <merge-base>` over the changed event files; a bug in path parsing (`ticket_id, filename = rel.split('/',1)`) or the diff-filter would only surface in production

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure at least one non-skippable test asserts the signed/verified path (e.g. an injected valid-signature fixture or a hard requirement/xfail marker instead of silent skip) so signing + `verified` + ledger consumption are always exercised.
evidence: `@pytest.mark.skipif(not _SSH_OK, reason="ssh-keygen >= 8.9 required")` guards test_snapshot_roundtrip_signed_events_still_verify
`_SSH_OK` is set False on any sshsig.ensure_available() exception (lines 24-28)
No non-skipped test asserts a `verified` count > 0 or that _apply_authorship sets event['author_sig'] (search: only the happy path asserts 'unsigned', advisory exit 0)
advisory.finding: The only test that produces a signed event and asserts a positive `verified` outcome / the snapshot authorship-ledger round-trip is guarded by `@pytest.mark.skipif(not _SSH_OK)`. On a runner lacking ssh-keygen >= 8.9 it skips, and NO other non-skipped test ever asserts that signing populates author_sig, that a signed event classifies `verified`, or that _build_authorship_ledger is consumed. The signing + verified-pass + ledger paths can then ship fully unexercised.
scenarios: CI/dev environment without a modern ssh-keygen: the entire signing/verified/ledger surface is untested while the suite still passes green

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `rebar fsck` output includes the aggregated 'authorship: X signed, Y unsigned' line and the verify-authorship suffix when unsigned events exist.
evidence: fsck.py adds `authorship_line = f"authorship: {signed_total} signed, {unsigned_total} unsigned event(s)"` and appends it
search of tests for `authorship:` yields no matches
advisory.finding: The new fsck advisory authorship line ('authorship: N signed, M unsigned event(s)' with the conditional '— run `rebar verify-authorship`' suffix) is added but has no test asserting fsck emits it or that the store-wide signed/unsigned totals aggregate correctly across tickets.
scenarios: A ticket's reduced `authorship` summary shape changes or the aggregation loop regresses; fsck output silently drops or miscounts the advisory

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bind ledger authorship entries to their event: recompute/verify canonical bytes (or verify the SNAPSHOT's own attestation over `authorship_ledger`) before trusting per-entry author_id/epoch in verify-authorship.
evidence: verify_authorship.py:127 `if ev.payload is not None and envelope.payload != ev.payload:` — binding only runs for live events
verify_authorship.py:177-179 ledger `_ScopedEvent` is built with `position=None, payload=None, epoch=entry.get("epoch")` — no recomputed canonical bytes
_ScopedEvent docstring (verify_authorship.py:55-57): 'payload ... (None for a ledger entry, where the raw event is gone and the envelope's own payload is trusted-at-compaction)'

attest/authorship.py:52-53 signature is taken over `dsse.pae(PAYLOAD_TYPE, payload)` — it binds the envelope payload but nothing ties that payload to the ledger entry's claimed event_uuid/author_id/epoch

verify_authorship.py:129-130 `if ev.epoch is not None: epoch = ev.epoch` — the epoch selecting valid keyring keys is taken directly from the attacker-writable ledger record, so a since-revoked key can be re-validated by choosing an older epoch
advisory.finding: The merge-gate skips content-binding for SNAPSHOT authorship_ledger entries: `_verify_signed` only checks `envelope.payload == ev.payload` when `ev.payload is not None`, but ledger entries are built with `payload=None`. The ledger's `author_id` and `epoch` are self-asserted snapshot fields verified in isolation, and the snapshot's own signature over the ledger is never checked here. An actor who can author/tamper a SNAPSHOT can transplant any validly-signed authorship envelope onto a ledger entry with an arbitrary event_uuid/content and it will classify as `verified`, defeating the merge-gate for all compacted (folded) events.
scenarios: A tampered or maliciously-rebuilt SNAPSHOT (compact/rebuild path) places a genuine older authorship envelope from identity A onto a ledger record describing a different (or forged) folded event; `verify-authorship` returns `verified` and CI passes.
A ledger entry pins `epoch` to a value where a later-revoked signing key was still valid, verifying a signature made by a key that should no longer be trusted.
advisory.suggested_fix: Do not treat ledger entries as content-bound-by-trust. Either (a) verify the SNAPSHOT event's own signature/attestation over compiled_state (including authorship_ledger) before consuming any ledger entry, or (b) store the signed canonical payload in the ledger and re-derive `ev.payload` so the same `envelope.payload != ev.payload` binding check runs for ledger events, and derive `epoch` from a trusted source rather than the ledger field.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not blanket-skip identity tickets in verify-authorship; exempt only the identity CREATE while still verifying KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE (or authenticate keyring mutations by another means).
evidence: verify_authorship.py:231-232 `if _is_gate_exempt_ticket(ticket_dir): continue` skips the ENTIRE ticket directory
verify_authorship.py:100 `_GATE_EXEMPT_TYPES = ("session_log", "code_review", "identity")`
verify_authorship.py:96-99 justification only covers the identity's own CREATE ('An identity's own CREATE is unsigned by construction'), not KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE
attest/authorship.py:135-156 `verify_authorship_at_epoch` builds the trust root from the identity's keyring records — the very state KEY events mutate
advisory.finding: `_collect_all` skips every event of gate-exempt ticket types including `identity`, but identity tickets carry KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE events that mutate the epoch-scoped keyring (the authorship trust root). Because the whole identity ticket is skipped, key-management events are never authorship-verified by the merge-gate, so unauthenticated/forged changes to who may sign are not caught by the gate that is supposed to enforce authenticated authorship.
scenarios: An attacker adds a KEY_ADD event to an identity ticket to introduce their own signing key; the merge-gate never examines identity-ticket events, so the injected trust root is not flagged, and subsequent events signed with the injected key verify.
advisory.suggested_fix: Narrow the exemption to per-event: skip only the identity's CREATE event, and require KEY_ADD/KEY_REVOKE events on an identity ticket to be verified (e.g. signed by an already-valid key on that identity's keyring at the prior epoch), rather than skipping the entire identity ticket.
